To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the X gene of French HBV strains is highly polymorphic and differs from the Far East ones; (2) HBV strains from patients presenting with HCC are different from those from patients with chronic hepatitis; (3) HBV strains with mutations at position 1792 are more prevalent in HCC.
The sequence of the HBV X gene in French patients differs from that of Far East origin strains by A to T at 1678 and G …
the HBV strains from patients born in the Lorraine region were different from the ones of the Far East origin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new polymorphism of the HBV X gene from patients with HCC and chronic hepatitis born in France.
the study of hepatitis B virus X gene from French‐born patients.
the study of the variability of the HBV X gene in patients born in Lorrain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the X protein is a multifunctional regulator that can either activate or repress transcription, depending on the cellular context and the viral stage of infection.
the HBV X gene is not a major determinant of hepatocarcinogenesis.
there is no evidence for a causal association between hepatitis B virus infection and hepatocellular cancer in the United States.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HBV X gene from patients from Lorraine is different from the Far East strains and the differences are located in the C‐terminus region of the gene.
the X gene of the HBV strains from Lorraine is highly polymorphic and the polymorphisms are located mainly in the central region of the gene.
the HBV X gene from patients with HCC and chronic hepatitis from the Lorraine region is highly conserved and is similar to that of other French isolates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the X gene of hepatitis B virus is highly polymorphic.
the X gene of hepatitis B viruses circulating in France has a different variability pattern compared with the Far East.
the X gene of hepatitis B virus is a promising target for the development of antivirals against the hepatitis B virus.
